replying_to: Replying to Questions on Tree Construction

content.comment:
Thanks for your comments.

Q1: Given your example, our combiner has the six output representations of the first layer, but (B and C), (D and E) have the same representations separately. For the next layer, if (A, B) is connected and shared, we treat it as A is connected to (B, C) and then (A, B, C) will share the same output representations.

Q2: We do not enforce binary trees for unsupervised parsing experiments. However, as shown in Figure 2, the learned attention gates for softmax weights tend to have a value larger than 0.5, which means it usually learns a binary connection.

Q3: In this work, our goal is to add language structures into the Transformer model as inductive bias, and we except the learning process is fully data-driven without extra human constraints. For regular language, we choose the unsupervised constituency parsing task to demonstrate that the learned structures in language are reasonable and explainable. There are some cases that our model learns skipped connections, which results in wrong tag detection. It is expected that adding constraints to prevent skip connections could lead to better parsing results. However, since the main goal is to demonstrate that the fully data-driven approach of inductively learned structures is effective and intuitive, we choose the more general setting and allow skip connections. In more complex scenarios like search sessions, the learned skipped connections can indeed help us model the unstructured search language (e.g., in Appendix A.4, we show there are some cross-query connections for search session data).

replying_to: Replying to Questions about the model details.

content.comment:
Thanks for your comments.

Q1: To obtain the tree structure from Combiner, we post-process the hierarchical attention block from the bottom layers to the top layers as shown in Figure 1 (b,c). We connect the token with kept attention weights in the sparse attention map at each layer until every input token is connected to the tree structure or the final layer is reached. After multiple token nodes are merged, they will be treated as a single node in the next round of merging at the following layers. In this way, we can obtain tree structures instead of graphs from Combiner.

Q2: The softmax operation is only based on the non-zero attention weights in Eqn 5.
